title: OxBlood: A Cyber Drill Platform
description: A Proxmox-backed cyber drill platform for managing repeatable red-team and blue-team exercises, scenario definitions, telemetry, and operational reporting.

sections.title: What I Built
content: This project turns a security lab into a repeatable exercise platform. It combines a web portal, API services, scenario schemas, database migrations, deployment configuration, and Proxmox integration into one operational workflow.
The platform is designed around controlled exercises rather than isolated demonstrations, making it possible to define scenarios, run drills, observe outcomes, and improve the next iteration.

sections.title: Architecture
content: The platform runs as a Docker Compose stack behind Traefik. A Flask portal serves the React interface and proxies API calls to a FastAPI backend. The backend keeps its state in PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO, and controls Proxmox VE to build and reset the training range. Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana watch the stack.

figure.alt: Architecture diagram: players and referees reach Traefik, the Flask portal and the FastAPI backend inside a Docker Compose stack. The backend uses PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO, and controls Proxmox VE, which hosts the red team, blue team and scenario machines. Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana provide observability.

sections.title: How a drill runs
content: A drill holds up to 20 players in 2, 4 or 6 teams. Rounds swap sides, so every team attacks once and defends once, and the points from all rounds are added up.

figure.alt: Flow diagram of a drill in seven steps: create the exercise, set up teams, plan rounds, prepare the range, start a round, play and score, then finish and reset. After the reset the next round starts again, and referees can adjust points with a written reason while a round is played.
figure.caption: The life of a drill, from creating the exercise to resetting the range between rounds.

bullets: Flags get a new value at the start of every round and are written to the machines first, so a flag from an earlier round never scores.
A flag scores once per team per round. Points decay over time, the first team to capture a flag gets a 25% bonus, and more than 10 attempts a minute are refused.
Referees can add or remove points only with a written reason, and every change stays in a ledger with the referee's name and the time.
With 4 or 6 teams, the one-range-per-match option gives each pair of teams its own copy of the range, with its own VLANs.
Between rounds every machine rolls back to its clean-baseline snapshot, boots, and is checked before the next round can start.

sections.title: Engineering and Security Value
content: Isolation is tested, not assumed. A script runs from inside the red-team machines and checks that the Proxmox web interface and SSH cannot be reached, and a dry-run tool builds a range, validates every VM and tears it down before an event.
The platform is built to be operated. It has a health endpoint, a database backup script, and Prometheus alert rules routed through Alertmanager to Discord, Telegram or email.
